articles.title: Git Bisect Explained: Find the Bad Commit in About 10 Checks
articles.excerpt: Git bisect explained: mark one bad commit and an older good one, and Git's binary search finds which of the last thousand commits broke your code in about ten checks, not one by one. Each answer throw…
articles.body: Git bisect explained: mark one bad commit and an older good one, and Git's binary search finds which of the last thousand commits broke your code in about ten checks, not one by one. Each answer throws out about half the suspects. In the manual's own example, 675 revisions left becomes 337, and that example goes back to Linus Torvalds's original git bisect commit from July 2005. Then the surprise: you don't have to answer yourself. git bisect run takes your test script and reads its exit code: 0 means good, 1 to 127 means bad, 125 means skip this commit, and anything above 127 stops the search.

articles.body: Before You Trust a Password Manager, Ask These Five Questions A password manager may store some of your most sensitive information. Choosing one should involve more than comparing features or looking at a security badge. website link: https://www.lockera.xyz/ Here are five useful questions to ask before trusting any password manager. 1. What is encrypted, and where? Look for a clear explanation of what data is encrypted, where encryption and decryption happen, and what information may still be visible to the service provider. A phrase like “encrypted” is a starting point. The details matter. 2. What happens if I forget my master password? Recovery can work differently from one product to another.

articles.title: Prevent Abandoned Payments and Cart State Loss in Vue 3 Telegram Mini Apps
articles.excerpt: When building an e-commerce catalog inside a Telegram Mini App using Vue 3, frontend state management requires a fundamental shift from traditional web apps. Telegram runs Mini Apps inside an embedded…
articles.body: When building an e-commerce catalog inside a Telegram Mini App using Vue 3, frontend state management requires a fundamental shift from traditional web apps. Telegram runs Mini Apps inside an embedded webview framework across iOS, Android, and Desktop clients. Mobile operating systems aggressively suspend or completely dispose of these webview contexts when a user toggles to another chat, answers an incoming call, or opens a native Telegram payment interface. If your Vue application relies solely on an in-memory Pinia store for cart management, a webview reload flushes the customer's selected items immediately. The customer returns to an empty cart or, worse, triggers a checkout with a stale or zero-value payload.

articles.title: Event-driven architecture for system design interviews, explained
articles.excerpt: Event-driven architecture for system design interviews, explained Split a system into services and you hit a fork: when an order is placed, does the order service call the payment, inventory and notif…
articles.body: Event-driven architecture for system design interviews, explained Split a system into services and you hit a fork: when an order is placed, does the order service call the payment, inventory and notification services and wait — or does it just announce "order placed" and let whoever cares react? That second answer is event-driven architecture (EDA) : services communicate by emitting and reacting to events through a broker, asynchronously, instead of calling each other directly.

articles.body: 📅 November 23, 2026 • Z.ai On November 23, 2026 Z.ai (also known as Zhipu AI) released GLM-5.4 , its first flagship model built on a Loop Transformer architecture. The design takes the 28 layers of the GLM-5 base model and runs them for two iterations per forward pass , giving a deeper network without adding parameters. Scale is about 750 billion parameters , and the company says intelligence is comparable to 2T-3T parameter models. Vision is added for visual coding — the model reads screenshots and images — and the context window is 1 million tokens . Access is live now for GLM Coding Plan subscribers in ZCode and Z.ai Chat, with the model name glm-5.4[1m] in Claude Code and glm-5.4 in other tools.

articles.title: Best Data Modeling Tools for Google BigQuery: SQLDBM, dbt, Dataform & Looker Compared
articles.excerpt: Modeling data in BigQuery is a different beast than modeling in Postgres or SQL Server. You've got nested STRUCTs, repeated fields, partitions, clustering, and labels to think about. On top of that, m…
articles.body: Modeling data in BigQuery is a different beast than modeling in Postgres or SQL Server. You've got nested STRUCTs, repeated fields, partitions, clustering, and labels to think about. On top of that, most teams now layer dbt or Dataform for transformations and Looker for BI, which means your "modeling tool" has to play nicely with three or four other systems. Pick wrong and you'll be hand-writing YAML and copy-pasting DDL for months. I spent a few weeks running the main options against real BigQuery datasets. I cared about three things: how well each tool handled BigQuery-native features, how much manual work it eliminated across the dbt and semantic-layer workflow, and whether a mixed team of architects, analysts, and business stakeholders could actually collaborate in it.

articles.excerpt: The vibration motor has more potential than Google allows.
articles.body: TL;DR Two unofficial apps bring notification and incoming call vibrations to the Fitbit Air. Cuff offers customizable alerts on Android, while AirBuzz uses iOS 27’s Shortcuts automations. Google doesn’t officially support either workaround, but both are available to try. Google designed the Fitbit Air for people who want to track their health without another screen competing for their attention. That philosophy explains why the band doesn’t display notifications or even vibrate when calls and messages arrive. But there’s a difference between avoiding constant distractions and wanting to know when something important needs your attention. Google hasn’t offered users that middle ground, so independent developers have stepped in.

articles.body: Encapsulate Inc. This Nov. 19, 2026, image shows gastric microtumors grown within an Encapsulates biochip. articles.title: The remains of a long-dead volcano on Mars | Space photo of the day for Nov. 23, 2026
articles.excerpt: Just imagine the ancient, Martian lava flowing.
articles.body: An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains.
